text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sixteen people killed in "terrorist" attacks in three regions and six others kidnapped by gunmen.
- Car bombs explode in Chlef, west of Algiers, and in Boumerdes, east of the Algerian capital.

- Political leaders continue campaigning for the June 5 parliamentary election: Said Saadi from the anti-Islamist Rally for Culture and Democracy says the "Algerian people is aware of the Islamist extremist agenda". Islamist-oriented Movement for a Peaceful Society said the country's economic crisis will be eased by the private sector.
- Expatriate Algerian voters start polling on Saturday ahead of next week's general election in Algeria.
- Abdelkader Bensalah, leader of the National Democratic Rally (RND), said his party aims to unify Algerian ranks to end the country's crisis.
- Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf, campaigning for the RND in central Ain Defla province, said "terrorism was defeated" in Algeria.
- Boualem Benhamouda, leader of the former ruling National Liberation Front, said his party is still strong and those who claim the FLN is dead are liars.
- "Terrorists" kill 11 villagers near Cherchell, west of Algiers.
- Secular Socialist Forces Front (FFS) said the country will be thrown into street violence if the authorities cheat in the elections.
- Former prime minister Redha Malek, spearheading his Republican National Alliance campaign, said Algeria is sitting on a volcano.
- France sends no observer to watch Algeria's poll.
